181|Low-cost, low-power SoC microcontrollers with Bluetooth and Wi-Fi
181@1-65:16 66-80:0
182|
182@1-80:0
183|ESP-WROOM-32 module with ESP32-D0WDQ6 chip
183@1-42:16 43-80:0
184|
184@1-80:0
185|
185@1-80:0
186|ESP32is a family of low-cost, energy-efficientmicrocontrollersthat support both
186@1-46:16 47-62:11 63-79:16 80-80:0
187|Wi-FiandBluetooth. These chips feature several processing options, including
187@1-5:11 6-8:16 9-17:11 18-77:16 78-80:0
188|theTensilicaXtensa LX6 microprocessor available in dual-core and single-core
188@1-3:16 4-12:11 13-77:16 78-80:0
189|variants, the Xtensa LX7 dual-core processor, or aRISC-Vmicroprocessor. The
189@1-50:16 51-56:11 57-76:16 77-80:0
190|ESP32 incorporates components for wireless data communication such as built-in
190@1-79:16 80-80:0
191|antenna switches, an RFbalun, power amplifiers, low-noise receivers, filters,
191@1-23:16 24-28:11 29-78:16 79-80:0
192|and power-management modules.
192@1-29:16 30-80:0
193|
193@1-80:0
194|Typically, the ESP32 is embedded on device-specificprinted circuit boards(PCBs)
194@1-51:16 52-73:11 74-80:16
195|or offered as part of development kits that include a variety ofGPIOpins and
195@1-64:16 65-68:11 69-77:16 78-80:0
196|connectors, with configurations varying by model and manufacturer. The ESP32
196@1-77:16 78-80:0
197|was designed byEspressif Systemsand is manufactured byTSMCusing their 40 nm
197@1-15:16 16-32:11 33-54:16 55-58:11 59-76:16 77-80:0
198|process.[2]It is a successor to theESP8266microcontroller.
198@1-8:16 9-11:11 12-35:16 36-42:11 43-58:16 59-80:0
